steps.title: Sémillon
steps.body: Hunter Sémillon is picked early, at about 10 to 11% alcohol, to avoid harvest rain and keep acidity. It's fermented cool in steel, without oak or malolactic, and bottled early. Young, it's pale, lean and lemony, with grass and high acidity. With 5 to 10 years in bottle, it transforms, gaining toast, honey, lanolin and lemon curd, as if oaked.
steps.highlight: Picked early, unoaked, transforms with age

steps.title: Shiraz
steps.body: Hunter Shiraz is medium-bodied, unlike the Barossa's, with red fruit, earth and a savoury, leathery character, sometimes called sweaty saddle in older wines. It's lower in alcohol, around 13 to 13.5%, and ages well. Chardonnay is also grown. Tyrrell's Vat 1 Sémillon and Vat 9 Shiraz are famous examples.

steps.prompt: Match each term to the Hunter.
steps.explanation: The Hunter's grapes have a distinct style.

steps.body: Hunter Sémillon's toasty notes after ten years come entirely from bottle age, not oak. It's one of wine's great transformations.

steps.prompt: Why is Hunter Sémillon picked so early?
options: To avoid harvest rain and keep acidity
steps.explanation: Early picking avoids rot and preserves freshness.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Hunter Sémillon is picked early, unoaked, and transforms with age
Hunter Shiraz is medium-bodied and earthy
Tyrrell's Vat 1 and Vat 9 are famous examples
